associations.rationale: Over an arbitrary type carrying a Field instance, the formal type states that every endomorphism of a finite-dimensional indecomposable module is bijective or nilpotent, directly giving the lemma's arbitrary-field form.
Over an arbitrary field, the formal type states existence of a decomposition of a finite-dimensional module into indecomposable submodules whose independent supremum is the whole module.
Over an arbitrary field, the formal type states uniqueness of two finite indecomposable direct-sum decompositions up to equal cardinality, permutation, and module equivalence.

The formal type proves that a finite sum of nilpotent endomorphisms of an indecomposable module is nilpotent; this is a helper result rather than the arbitrary-field lemma or Krull-Schmidt statement itself.
